annotation.title_clean: Towards Responsible AI Innovation: Second INTERPOL-UNICRI Report on Artificial Intelligence for Law Enforcement
annotation.title_en: Towards Responsible AI Innovation: Second INTERPOL-UNICRI Report on Artificial Intelligence for Law Enforcement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UNICRI (Centre for AI and Robotics) and INTERPOL (Innovation Centre)
annotation.summary_en: Joint INTERPOL-UNICRI report from the 2019 Singapore meeting on AI for law enforcement. It covers AI domains, national use cases, legal and ethical considerations (GDPR, LED, FATE principles), and proposes a non-binding Responsible AI Innovation Toolkit and roadmap. Embodied AI appears only in passing, as malicious drones.
key_provisions_or_claims: Responsible AI use by police should rest on human rights, democracy, justice and rule of law, operationalised via fairness, accountability, transparency and explainability.
GDPR and the Law Enforcement Directive (Art. 11 on automated decisions) are key legal instruments for police AI.
Proposes a non-binding, operational toolkit for responsible AI innovation in law enforcement.
Recommends a statement of principles, an expert advisory committee, external audit support and guidance on court admissibility of AI.
Stresses public trust and social acceptance, and warns of malicious AI use such as deepfakes and drones.
